harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured inventory-api as a boot-enabled SysV service on TCP 8080. The batchworker account has a 128 MB per-process virtual-memory limit. Oversized allocations fail without interrupting the API. Node1 rebooted successfully, received a new boot ID, and all configuration and services recovered on Ubuntu 7.10 with the original kernel.
actions_performed: Created dedicated inventory-api and batchworker accounts.
Installed a Python 2.5-compatible inventory API with health and inventory endpoints.
Created and enabled the inventory-api SysV init service.
Applied a 131072 KiB soft and hard address-space limit to batchworker through PAM limits.
Verified that a 192 MB batchworker allocation fails with MemoryError while the API remains healthy.
Safely rebooted node1 once and verified boot identity changed and service recovery completed.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api is a managed service on TCP port 8080
evidence.summary: Shows enabled SysV startup links, a TCP 8080 listener, HTTP 200 API responses, and automatic service recovery after reboot.

evidence.requirement: batchworker is limited to 128 MB virtual memory per process without interrupting the API
evidence.summary: Shows the 131072 KiB soft/hard limit, runtime enforcement via MemoryError, and an unchanged healthy API process before and after failed allocations, including after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Legacy operating-system release and kernel were retained
evidence.summary: Confirms Ubuntu 7.10, Python 2.5 compatibility, and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic after completion.

Captures healthy pre-restart state with boot ID 048decac-c4fc-429b-8ebe-967f1455e64f, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID 580bb1f0-d43d-4459-822b-009b16c02d29, and recovered service, listener, API data, and batchworker limit.
